newsitem.title: UK: New head of Irish Roman Catholics installed.
newsitem.headline: New head of Irish Roman Catholics installed.

text.p: Archbishop Sean Brady was installed as the new leader of Irish Catholics on Sunday and said the need for reconciliation on the island was urgent.
"The most urgent religious task of our day is the search for peace and reconciliation," Brady said at a ceremony in Armagh Cathedral.

"Reconciliation is not something to be put on a long finger. It is not something to be attempted only after a political solution has been found. It is not a task for religious leaders alone. It belongs to all men and women of goodwill," he said.
Irish President Mary Robinson, members of the Irish government and Britain's Northern Ireland Secretary, Sir Patrick Mayhew, were among 1,000 guests at the ceremony.
Brady was named successor to Cardinal Cahal Daly in December 1994.
He takes over at a time when the Roman Catholic church in Ireland has been hit by a series of sexual scandals involving the clergy and children.
Reports of child molestation have become regular front-page news across the island of Ireland, which has a population of around four million Catholics.

Brady, 57, has said he wants the Irish Republican Army (IRA), an underground guerrilla group which fights to end British rule of Northern Ireland, to call a new ceasefire which would allow its Sinn Fein political wing entry to peace talks.
He told a news conference last week that the people of Ireland yearned for an end to the 27-year Northern Ireland conflict and hoped to see it.

"My personal conviction about this is derived from the deep longing for peace which is palpable throughout the entire community. The overwhelming majority of people reject the path of violence," he said.
Brady is a farmer's son from County Cavan, on the Irish border with Northern Ireland.
He was educated at St Patrick's college in Maynooth, outside Dublin, and went on to the Irish College in Rome, where he earned a doctorate in divinity.
Brady was ordained in 1964 at the age of 24 and was a priest at Castletara in County Cavan.
